name: Simon
overview: The name Simon appears in Scripture referring to several distinct individuals, each with unique roles and backgrounds. Among them is Simon the Canaanite, also called Simon the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles known for his fervent patriotism (Matthew 10:4; Mark 3:18). Another Simon is identified as a physical half-brother of Jesus, mentioned alongside Jesus' other brothers, highlighting Jesus' earthly family ties (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3). Additionally, Simon the leper is noted as someone with whom Jesus dined, illustrating Jesus' ministry to those marginalized by society (Matthew 26:6). The name also belongs to a man from Cyrene compelled to carry Jesus' cross, emphasizing the participation of others in Christ's passion (Matthew 27:32). These references collectively show the varied ways God used men named Simon in the unfolding of the gospel narrative.
